_comment: The single place the native apps get their identity from. Read by capacitor.config.ts, by android/app/build.gradle, and by scripts/mobile-identity.mjs, so an identifier can never be right in one project and wrong in the other. NOT YET REGISTERED with either store — see `registered` below.
_appName_comment: The name that appears under the icon on a phone's home screen, and nowhere else. It is title-cased — Hangyul Ganada — because a launcher label sits beside Photos, Maps and Settings, and a lowercased second word reads there as a typo rather than as the deliberate lowercase of 가나다. The prose product name in the app, the store listing and every document stays `Hangyul ganada`; scripts/check-product-name.mjs enforces that split, and scripts/check-mobile-identity.mjs enforces that Android's strings.xml and iOS's Info.plist both carry exactly this value. Changing the name here and nowhere else is the supported way to rename the installed app.

registered._comment: Set each to true only once the identifier has actually been created in the corresponding console. Nothing in the build depends on these; they exist so the release checklist cannot be answered from memory.

_version_comment: 1.0.3, unchanged. Build 14 replaces the two platform application logos, declares an answer domain on every Numbers item so an option list can only hold one kind of thing, and adds the deterministic answer-equivalence module. None of that is a new feature set, so the version name stays where it is and only the build number moves.
_buildNumber_comment: 14, because 13 is spent. The delivered AAB and APK in result/ and app_result/ both report versionCode 13 and build-info.json records 13, and product files have changed since the commit that produced them — every launcher and app-store icon, the Numbers question model and seven new items with their recordings, and the korean-morphology equivalence module. A rebuild at 13 would put different bytes under a code a set of bytes already exists for. `npm run version:check` is what said so, before the build rather than after. Nothing has been uploaded to Play (see `registered.googlePlay`), so 14 is the next valid code rather than the next unused one. This number is set by a person deciding to ship, never incremented by a script or a tool run.

android._comment: targetSdk 36 because Google Play requires Android 16 for new apps and updates from 31 August 2026. minSdk 24 is Capacitor 8's floor and covers ~99% of active devices.

xcode._comment: What `App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` currently carries, written down here so that a check can tell a *deliberate lag* from a *drift*. The Xcode project is maintained on a Mac, by hand, through the Xcode UI: MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION are build settings Xcode owns, and editing them from Linux with a text substitution is how a project file loses a setting it was never asked about. So this release moves Android to 1.0.3 build 11 and leaves iOS where its maintainer left it. `scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs` asserts the project file matches these two values exactly — any other change to it fails — and prints the pending action while they are behind `version` and `buildNumber`.
xcode.pending: iOS is behind: set MARKETING_VERSION to 1.0.3 and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION to 12 in Xcode (App target, both configurations), then update the two values above in the same commit.

ios._comment: 15.0 to match IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in the Xcode project — the two disagreeing is how a build succeeds and then crashes on a device the store said it supported. Capacitor 8's own floor is 14; 15 is chosen because it is what the project is configured for and covers every device Apple still updates. Apple requires builds made with the iOS 26 SDK from 28 April 2026; that is the SDK you build *with*, not the version you deploy *to*.
